text: I went to get a molar extracted on Friday evening. The dentist was in a hurry, injected the local anesthetic, had me rinse my mouth, and then started extracting. They asked if I felt the anesthetic, and I said it wasn't quite numb yet. The nurse then asked if I felt my lip getting thicker, and I said no, not at all. They adjusted the chair and started the extraction. In short, it hurt. I was in so much pain I tensed up. I told the dentist it hurt, and they seemed annoyed, probably because they were in a rush. They used an instrument to test the other side and explained what pain felt like. I understand, but they should understand the patient's perspective – the anesthetic hadn't fully numbed everything yet. After the extraction, I was shaking and crying in the clinic. The total cost for the extraction was 1,240 baht.

restaurant_name: คลินิกเจริญกรุงทันตแพทย์
text:
I went to the male dentist in room 1 on Sunday. I saw him twice. He didn't answer my questions; his assistant answered instead, and he did it hastily, then went to type it on the computer.

I needed him to drill my tooth because it was cracked and so sharp it had cut my tongue, causing pain. I asked the assistant, "If the pain subsides but the tooth is still sharp, can I come back to get it fixed?" The assistant replied, "That means the tooth has cracked further." I said, "Shouldn't I wait until the pain subsides?" I asked twice, and he gave the same answer. It was as if he wanted my tooth to crack further if it remained sharp. And now, the pain is starting to subside. I also feel like he didn't completely remove the sharp edges. He's trying to make me pay extra, even though the procedure took only 5 seconds and cost 500 + 40 baht. I don't have insurance.

I've paid cash every time. This time I paid 500 + 40 baht, and he said he couldn't find my patient record. Five people who came after me were already treated, and I was the last one, waiting for an hour even though I arrived early.
